name: Porvoo
title: Porvoo Tanker Gauging: Thickness Measurement at Sköldvik
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement for crude, product, chemical and gas tankers at Porvoo's Sköldvik harbour: deck, piping, ballast tank and hull UTM.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Tankers at the Kilpilahti Refinery Harbour, Porvoo
intro: Porvoo's shipping is concentrated at Sköldvik, the harbour of the Kilpilahti industrial area, where Neste runs Finland's only oil refinery next to a Borealis petrochemical plant. Crude tankers, product and chemical tankers and gas carriers come and go all year, and by tonnage the harbour ranks among the busiest in the country. Gauging on these ships is planned around cargo transfer and strict terminal rules. For each Porvoo job, our technicians make the journey from India to the tanker.

highlights.p: Crude tankers discharging feedstock and product tankers loading fuels give the longest stays at Sköldvik. Deck plating, the outside of cargo and ballast piping, and certified-safe voids can be measured under the ship's permit system while transfer goes on.

Tankers serving Porvoo in winter cross the Gulf of Finland with icebreaker support. High ice classes are common in this fleet, and ice-belt readings before and after the season show how much of the abrasion allowance is left.

highlights.h: ESP and CAP for ageing tankers
highlights.p: Oil and chemical tankers come under the Enhanced Survey Programme, and charterers of older ships often ask for a CAP rating. A pre-docking estimate taken at Porvoo helps the owner plan the gas-free gauging those surveys will demand.

port.h: Sköldvik: the refinery harbour on the Gulf of Finland
p: Porvoo itself is a historic small town east of Helsinki, but its commercial shipping uses Sköldvik, a harbour to the south on the coast of the Kilpilahti industrial area. That harbour exists for the refinery and petrochemical complex behind it: crude oil and other feedstocks come in by sea, and petrol, diesel, jet fuel, renewable fuels, liquefied gases and petrochemical products go out. Neste operates the harbour, with a set of berths for liquid and gas cargoes and the jetties, loading arms and safety systems that go with them. Because the complex lies on the Gulf of Finland coast, ships reach it by a short approach from the main shipping lane rather than a long archipelago fairway, although pilotage applies as at every Finnish port.

The fleet is almost entirely tankers and gas carriers. Crude carriers bring feedstock from distant loading terminals, and product tankers carry refined fuels to Finnish coastal depots, the Baltic states, Scandinavia and north-west Europe. Chemical tankers and gas carriers serve the petrochemical plant, moving olefins and other chemicals to and from the site. Tankers here face some of the most demanding winter conditions of any regular tanker trade, because the Gulf of Finland ices over in normal winters and the refinery has to be supplied regardless, so ice-strengthened tankers, many of them built for this kind of service, have long been a feature of the route. That combination of heavy cargo service and annual ice is what makes the steel on these ships worth watching closely.

Port stays at Sköldvik are set by the transfer. A crude discharge or a product loading takes long enough for a defined gauging scope, but the ship is working cargo throughout, so the team operates under both the ship's permit system and the harbour's safety rules, with hot work out of the question and access to hazardous zones restricted. Inside the cargo tanks nothing can be done until the ship is gas-free, which happens at a repair yard or during a planned gas-free period, not alongside the refinery. In winter, Finnish traffic restrictions set the ice class needed for assistance to Porvoo, and escorts can change arrival times. Ships waiting for a jetty anchor off the coast when ice allows, and are boarded by launch.

facilities.h: Where tankers calling at Porvoo can be gauged
p: Alongside the Sköldvik jetties, gauging is confined to what can be done safely during cargo operations. Typical areas are main-deck plating and longitudinals, the outside of cargo, ballast, vapour and fire-main piping on deck, the pump room where the ship's procedures allow, the engine room and sea-water systems, and ballast tanks or void spaces that the crew has ventilated and certified for entry. Equipment brought aboard has to satisfy the hazardous-area rules the ship and the harbour apply, and the team's documents and safety induction are cleared through the agent before the berthing.

There is no ship repair yard at Porvoo or Sköldvik, so dry-docking and the gas-free work that goes with it take place elsewhere: in Finland at Naantali or Rauma, or at yards in Poland, the Baltic states and further afield. Measuring deck, piping and accessible ballast tanks at Porvoo before the docking gives the yard a partial steel list and shows which cargo tanks deserve the closest look once they are opened. Product tankers trading regularly between Porvoo and coastal depots can have the work spread over several calls, so that little is left for the yard.
list: Sköldvik crude and product jetties — deck plating, deck piping exteriors and engine-room systems on tankers during transfer
Gas and chemical berths serving the petrochemical plant — ballast tanks, voids and deck structure outside hazardous zones
Repeat calls by coastal product tankers — deck and piping programmes spread over several visits
Anchorage off Sköldvik — tankers waiting for a jetty, boarded by launch when ice and weather allow
Docking yards at Naantali, Rauma and across the Baltic — cargo tank and bottom gauging once the ship is gas-free and dry

context.h: Tanker survey rules, ice and the refinery's direction
p: Ships at Sköldvik are subject to Paris MoU port state control, which Traficom, the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, carries out, and tankers rank among the higher-risk ship types in the Paris MoU targeting system when their age and record warrant it, so corrosion and structural defects on deck are among the first things an inspector sees. Oil tankers are surveyed under IACS UR Z10.1 or Z10.4 depending on their hull arrangement, and chemical tankers under Z10.3; their intermediate and renewal surveys under the Enhanced Survey Programme set out mandatory thickness measurement and close-up survey that widen with every cycle. Charterers of older tankers commonly add CAP, and oil majors' vetting inspections look hard at deck and piping condition, which pushes owners to measure before a problem appears in a report.

Ice and the energy transition are the two forces particular to Porvoo. Under the Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules, tankers that must reach the refinery through a hard Gulf of Finland winter need high ice classes, and the ice-belt plating and frames that earn those classes lose steel to abrasion every season. At the same time, Neste has announced plans to move its Porvoo operations towards renewable and circular raw materials, which will change the mix of cargoes and ships over time. Emissions from tanker voyages between Porvoo and other EU ports fall under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, and every tanker calling must keep its Inventory of Hazardous Materials current under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation.

jobs.p: Porvoo jobs are tanker jobs, and their shape is set by what cannot be done alongside. The usual brief is to measure everything accessible during transfer, so that when the ship reaches a yard or a gas-free window the remaining scope is known and smaller. Owners preparing for a second or third renewal survey, a CAP rating or a sale use Porvoo calls to gather deck, piping and ballast tank figures early. Regular coastal product tankers have their programmes split over repeated calls. Gas carriers bring narrower scopes because of their hazardous zones, but their ballast tanks and deck structure still yield useful readings.
list: Deck plating, deck longitudinals and cargo and ballast pipe exteriors on an ice-class product tanker loading at Sköldvik, ahead of its renewal survey
Ballast tank gauging on a crude tanker during discharge, in tanks the crew has ventilated and certified for entry
Groundwork for a CAP survey on an older chemical tanker: deck, piping and accessible ballast spaces measured at the berth
Ice-belt readings from inside the forepeak and wing ballast tanks of a tanker after a hard winter
Sea-water and fire-main piping in the engine room of a gas carrier during a loading call
Pre-purchase gauging on a product tanker within the harbour's permit rules, with gas-free spaces added where available

logistics: Helsinki-Vantaa Airport is close to Porvoo, and the team reaches Sköldvik by road. The refinery harbour is a high-security industrial site: the ship's agent submits the team's details, arranges passes and the harbour's safety induction before the call, and books a launch if the tanker is at anchor. Technicians travelling from India need a Schengen visa for Finland, so we confirm dates against the tanker's laycan or berthing window as early as possible and keep a margin for consular processing.

faqs.q: Can cargo tanks be gauged while a tanker is alongside at Sköldvik?
faqs.a: Not from inside. Entering cargo tanks requires the ship to be gas-free, with an entry certificate from a competent person, and that does not happen alongside a working refinery jetty. What can be done during transfer is deck structure, piping exteriors, the engine room and ballast tanks or voids certified safe. Cargo tank structure is measured at the yard or during a planned gas-free period.

faqs.q: What equipment restrictions apply at the refinery harbour?
faqs.a: The harbour and the ship apply hazardous-area rules, so any equipment taken on deck has to meet them, and work is planned away from zones where it is not permitted. Ultrasonic thickness gauges are small battery-powered instruments, but they still go through the ship's and the harbour's acceptance. We send equipment details through the agent with the team's documents so nothing is turned back at the gate.

faqs.q: Is a Porvoo call useful before a tanker's renewal survey?
faqs.a: Yes. Deck plating, longitudinals, deck piping and accessible ballast tanks make up a large part of a tanker's renewal-survey thickness measurement, and measuring them at Porvoo reduces what must be done once the ship is gas-free in dock. It also gives an early view of where substantial corrosion lies, so the yard can be briefed on likely steel renewal before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: How does winter affect tanker jobs at Porvoo?
faqs.a: Tankers keep calling through the winter, but icebreaker escort in the Gulf of Finland can move the arrival, and launches to the anchorage may be limited in heavy ice. We plan the team's travel around the confirmed berthing and allow a day of margin. Work in tanks, the engine room and covered spaces continues normally, while open-deck work is shortened by cold and short daylight in midwinter.

faqs.q: Do you gauge the ice belt on tankers calling at Porvoo?
faqs.a: We measure the ice belt from inside wherever access allows, through the forepeak, wing ballast tanks and side spaces, and compare the readings with the original and minimum thicknesses from the ship's drawings. External readings on the shell are best taken in dry dock. Judging whether the ice class is still satisfied is for the class surveyor; our role is to supply the measured figures.
